lines.text: Many learners say: I will call you when I will arrive.
Better: I will call you when I arrive.
Arrive! Call me when you arrive.

data.wrong: I will call you when I will arrive.
data.right: I will call you when I arrive.

en.hook: Do you say “when I will arrive”?
en.tip: After “when”, we use the present, not the future.
en.caption: Watch out for this common mistake! Many people say “I will call you when I will arrive.”. The right way is “I will call you when I arrive.”. Unlike Portuguese, which uses a future form. Listen to Carlos and repeat! Practice more in the Lexkite app.
